# [Baseline] - WIN - D - Shared Device Name

Gives shared Windows devices a recognisable name: the customer abbreviation, SHR and the serial number, for example BC-SHR-7HQ2KX3. Takes effect after the next restart.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | Windows |
| Scope | Device (D) — assign to device groups |
| Type | Device config |
| Assignment | — |
| Source | Own baseline — Accounts CSP, Domain/ComputerName = %CustomerShort%-SHR-%SERIAL%. %CustomerShort% is a CIPP custom variable per customer; Windows fills in %SERIAL%. |
| File | [`Baseline_WIN_D_Shared_Device_Name.json`](Baseline_WIN_D_Shared_Device_Name.json) |

> Belongs on SG-D-UEM-WIN-Shared. First set the CIPP custom variable CustomerShort for the customer (at most 3 characters, letters and digits only): without it the device gets %CustomerShort% literally in its name and Windows refuses it. Windows keeps the name at 15 characters (NetBIOS) by cutting the serial number from the front: BC-SHR- leaves 8 characters of the serial number, ABC-SHR- 7. The new name only applies after a restart; Intune does not restart the device itself. Not for hybrid joined devices (the Accounts CSP does not support them). Choosing another name later renames every shared device again at its next restart.
